tests.name: Numerical Reasoning Test 2
tests.subtitle: AssessmentDay source test
tests.description: A 30-question mixed-difficulty numerical reasoning test based on six AssessmentDay data sets covering casino revenue, R&D, shareholdings, house sales, regional sales and European GDP.
tests.instructions:
This numerical reasoning test comprises 30 questions, and you will have 30 minutes in which to correctly answer as many as you can. Calculators are permitted for this test, and it is recommended you have some rough paper to work on.

You will have to work quickly and accurately to perform well in this test. If you don't know the answer to a question, leave it and come back to it if you have time. Each question will have five possible answers, one of which is correct. You may click Back and Next during the test to review or skip questions.

You can submit your test at any time. If the time limit is up before you click submit the test will automatically be submitted with the answers you have selected. It is recommended to keep working until the time limit is up.

Try to find a time and place where you will not be interrupted during the test. The test will begin on the next page.

questions.prompt: How much did the combined revenue from Slot machines and Roulette differ from that of Other table games between 2006-2009 inclusive (in £millions)?
questions.explanation: Roulette totals 0.8 + 0.6 + 0.6 + 0.7 = 2.7 and Slot machines total 1.3 + 1.4 + 1.8 + 1.5 = 6.0, so together they total 8.7 units of £100,000. Other table games total 4.4 + 4.2 + 4.5 + 4.8 = 17.9 units. The difference is 17.9 - 8.7 = 9.2 units of £100,000 = £0.92 million. Answer D.

questions.prompt: What was the average amount gambled on Slot machines in 2007 by each individual who attended Calewall casino?
questions.explanation: The 2007 Slot machine revenue was 1.4 × £100,000 = £140,000 and attendance was 15.2 × 100,000 = 1,520,000 people. £140,000 ÷ 1,520,000 = £0.0921, which rounds to £0.09. Answer E.

questions.prompt: There is a £15 entrance fee for each person gambling at Calewall casino. In which year, or years, was the entrance fee revenue less than £23 million?
questions.explanation: Entrance revenue is attendance × 100,000 × £15. For 2006 it is 14.6 × 100,000 × £15 = £21.9 million; for 2007 it is £22.8 million; for 2008 it is £24.45 million; for 2009 it is £25.2 million; and for 2010 it is £24.75 million. Only 2006 and 2007 are below £23 million. Answer A.

questions.prompt: What will be the average annual change in attendance at Calewall casino across the years 2006-2010 if the 2010 prediction proves to be accurate?
questions.explanation: Attendance changes from 14.6 × 100,000 in 2006 to 16.5 × 100,000 in 2010, a rise of 1.9 × 100,000 = 190,000 over four annual intervals. 190,000 ÷ 4 = 47,500, so the average annual change is a 47,500 increase. Answer D.

questions.prompt: Calewall casino is subject to a takeover bid of 7 times its 2010 projected casino revenues. The Board responds that it can deliver 10% added value through cost-cuttings to this purchase price. What valuation is the Board putting on Calewall casino (in £ millions)?
questions.explanation: Projected 2010 revenue is (0.5 + 1.1 + 4.7) × £100,000 = £630,000 = £0.63 million. The bid is 7 × £0.63 million = £4.41 million. Adding 10% gives £4.41 million × 1.10 = £4.851 million, or £4.85 million. Answer C.

questions.prompt: If the 2010 prediction proves to be accurate, what is the average annual percentage change in Teala Media’s R&D spend across the 5 years shown?
questions.explanation: Average the five displayed annual percentage changes: (2.6 + 1.6 - 1.8 - 0.8 + 1.2) ÷ 5 = 2.8 ÷ 5 = 0.56. Answer D.

questions.prompt: What is the R&D spend projected to be for 2010?
questions.explanation: The 2009 projects total £(425.9 + 672.8 + 215.5 + 1,056.0 + 113.2) thousand = £2,483.4 thousand. Applying the projected 1.2% rise gives £2,483.4 thousand × 1.012 = £2,513.201 thousand, approximately £2.5 million. Answer A.

questions.prompt: What was the R&D spend for 2008 (to the nearest £1,000)?
questions.explanation: The £2,483.4 thousand 2009 spend is 0.8% below 2008, so it equals 99.2% of the 2008 spend. £2,483.4 thousand ÷ 0.992 = £2,503.427 thousand, which rounds to £2,503,000. Answer C.

questions.prompt: R&D overheads were 12% of R&D spend in 2009. If R&D overheads are projected to rise by 1.1% between 2009 and 2010, what is the 2010 predicted R&D sum left after these overheads are taken in to account?
questions.explanation: 2009 overheads were £2.4834 million × 12% = £0.298008 million. After a 1.1% rise they are £0.298008 million × 1.011 = £0.301286 million. Predicted 2010 R&D spend is £2.4834 million × 1.012 = £2.513201 million, leaving £2.513201 million - £0.301286 million = £2.211915 million, or £2.21 million. Answer D.

questions.prompt: If delays at the end of 2009 resulted in a 2.5% increase in the cost of each of the two most expensive projects, what is the total R&D spend for 2009 (to the nearest £1,000)?
questions.explanation: The original total is £2,483.4 thousand. The two most expensive projects cost £1,056.0 thousand and £672.8 thousand, so the increase is (£1,056.0 + £672.8) thousand × 2.5% = £43.22 thousand. The revised total is £2,526.62 thousand, which rounds to £2,527,000. Answer B.

questions.prompt: What is the number of shares not held by Directors of Leutts (as of 30 April 2009)?
questions.explanation: Directors held 1,050 + 950 + 820 + 1,100 + 960 = 4,880 shares on 30 April. This is 16% of all shares, so total shares = 4,880 ÷ 0.16 = 30,500. Shares not held by Directors = 30,500 - 4,880 = 25,620. Answer A.

questions.prompt: Which Director has bought or sold the largest number of shares across the 2-month period shown?
questions.explanation: Compare 1 April with 31 May: Geoffrey Yates changed by -190, Tobey Gilham by -230, Susan Preddy by -700, Samantha Hoxton by -440, and Trudy Stupples by +1,200 shares. The largest absolute change is 1,200 shares for Trudy Stupples. Answer B.

questions.prompt: If Tobey Gilham sells half of his shareholding at 31 May 2009 at £45 per share, how much is this trade worth?
questions.explanation: Tobey Gilham held 820 shares on 31 May. Half is 820 ÷ 2 = 410 shares, and 410 × £45 = £18,450. Answer C.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true?
options: Current employees and Directors owned 40% of Leutts shares on 30 April 2009
The largest Director share dealing was 1,440 shares
Directors held 4,870 shares in total on 30 April 2009
Tobey Gilham held the most shares of any Director on 1st April 2009
Each Director has less shares on 31 May 2009 compared to 1st April 2009
questions.explanation: From 30 April to 31 May, Trudy Stupples increased her holding from 960 to 2,400, a dealing of 2,400 - 960 = 1,440 shares, so B is true. The other statements fail: employees plus Directors owned 21% + 16% = 37%; Directors held 4,880 shares on 30 April; Trudy, not Tobey, held the most on 1 April; and Trudy had more shares on 31 May than on 1 April.

questions.prompt: If Leutts shares are worth £52 on 30 April 2009, then what is the share valuation of the entire company?
questions.explanation: The 4,880 Director shares represent 16% of the company, giving 4,880 ÷ 0.16 = 30,500 total shares. At £52 each, the company valuation is 30,500 × £52 = £1,586,000. Answer D.

questions.prompt: The total number of £400,000 Apline houses sold in 2009 represented 80% of the annual sales target. If this target was split equally across 5 salerooms, what was the individual sales target for each salesroom?
questions.explanation: £400,000 house sales were 230 + 270 = 500. If 500 is 80% of target, the target is 500 ÷ 0.80 = 625. Split across five salerooms, 625 ÷ 5 = 125. Answer C.

questions.prompt: Stamp duty of 3% is paid on house sales over £250,000. How much stamp duty is paid by purchasers of Apline houses in 2009?
questions.explanation: Only £300,000, £400,000 and £500,000 houses qualify. Duty is 950 × £300,000 × 3% = £8.55 million, plus 500 × £400,000 × 3% = £6.00 million, plus 325 × £500,000 × 3% = £4.875 million. Total duty = £19.425 million. Answer C.

questions.prompt: What is the total value of 2009 Apline house sales?

In 2010, Apline house sales between Jan-June remain the same as those in 2009, while the sales for the July-Dec period increase by a fifth. What is the difference in Apline house sales between July-Dec 2010 and Jan-June for 2010 (in £million)?
questions.explanation: Jan-June 2009 value is 310 × £200,000 + 460 × £300,000 + 230 × £400,000 + 150 × £500,000 = £367.0 million. July-Dec 2009 value is £410.5 million, so July-Dec 2010 is £410.5 million × 1.20 = £492.6 million. The difference is £492.6 million - £367.0 million = £125.6 million. Answer E.

questions.prompt: A marketing drive is to be used to increase the value of Jan-June house sales to the value of July-December house sales. If each £ spent on marketing results in £3 of increased sales, what value must be spent on marketing?
questions.explanation: Jan-June sales are worth £367.0 million and July-December sales are worth £410.5 million, a gap of £43.5 million. At £3 of added sales per £1 of marketing, required spend is £43.5 million ÷ 3 = £14.5 million. Answer E.

questions.prompt: If the sales projections for next year prove accurate, which region will have maintained or increased sales levels each year from the previous year to next year?
questions.explanation: Northern sales are £310 million, £310 million and £320 million: they do not fall in either transition. Every other region falls in at least one transition. Answer A.

questions.prompt: What is the absolute difference between the lowest and the highest performing region (to the nearest £million) in the current year?
questions.explanation: In the current year the highest region is Northern at £310 million and the lowest is Central at £90 million. The absolute difference is £310 million - £90 million = £220 million. Answer E.

questions.prompt: If next year’s forecasts are scaled back by a quarter for the Northern and Western region, and by a fifth for the Southern and Eastern regions, what will be the total projected sales for all 5 regions?
questions.explanation: Adjusted projections are Northern 320 × 0.75 = 240, Western 270 × 0.75 = 202.5, Southern 165 × 0.80 = 132, Eastern 275 × 0.80 = 220, and unchanged Central = 125, all in £millions. Total = 240 + 202.5 + 132 + 220 + 125 = £919.50 million. Answer C.

questions.prompt: What were the ratios for the Central: Eastern regional sales for the Previous Year compared to the Current Year?
questions.explanation: Previous Year Central:Eastern is 110:290, which simplifies to 11:29. Current Year is 90:300, which simplifies to 3:10. Answer D.

questions.prompt: Put the regions in increasing order of total combined sales for the current year and next year’s projection
questions.explanation: Current plus projected sales are Central 90 + 125 = 215, Southern 160 + 165 = 325, Western 280 + 270 = 550, Eastern 300 + 275 = 575, and Northern 310 + 320 = 630, all in £millions. Increasing order is Central, Southern, Western, Eastern, Northern. Answer A.

questions.prompt: In which year (or years) was there more than a 3.3% difference in the GDP per person for France compared to the UK?
Which of the following statements is false?
options: Germany has the highest GDP of the countries shown.
Germany’s GDP is over 20% higher than the France’s GDP in 2009.
The 2005-2009 range of UK GDP per person is £23,500-£24,500.
The average GDP per country for the 5 countries shown is £2.18 billion.
The lowest and highest GDP per person are £20,500 and £25,700 respectively.
questions.explanation: The UK line ranges from £22,000 to £24,000, not £23,500 to £24,500, so C is false. The other statements check out: Germany has the highest GDP; (3.1 - 2.4) ÷ 2.4 = 29.17%; mean GDP is (2.4 + 3.1 + 1.95 + 1.4 + 2.05) ÷ 5 = £2.18 billion; and the 2009 per-person extremes are £20,500 and £25,700.

questions.prompt: Which two countries had the smallest difference in GDP per person in 2009?
questions.explanation: The 2009 values in £thousands are France 24.5, Germany 25.7, Italy 23.6, Spain 20.5 and UK 24.0. The smallest listed difference is UK versus Italy: 24.0 - 23.6 = £0.4 thousand. Answer A.

questions.prompt: Of those shown, between which years were the GDPs per person increasing in both France and the UK?
questions.explanation: France rises from £24,000 to £24,500 and the UK rises from £23,000 to £24,000 between 2008 and 2009. In every other interval at least one country falls. Answer A.

questions.prompt: What was the 2010 percentage change in the value of the Pacific Rim holding between October and November (to the nearest percent)?
questions.explanation: October Pacific Rim holdings were 20% × £37.5 million = £7.5 million. November holdings were 50.0 × £100,000 = £5.0 million. The decrease was (£7.5 million - £5.0 million) ÷ £7.5 million = 33.33%, or 33% less. Answer E.

questions.prompt: What was the ratio of Pacific Rim: Southern Pacific holdings in October 2010?
questions.explanation: The October pie gives Pacific Rim as 20% and Southern Pacific as 35%. The ratio 20:35 simplifies by 5 to 4:7. Answer E.

questions.prompt: In October 2010 which two Pacific Bond fund holdings when combined had the same value as Southern Pacific holdings?
questions.explanation: Southern Pacific is 35% of the fund. Central Pacific plus Pacific Rim is 15% + 20% = 35%, so the values are equal. Answer B.

questions.prompt: Which of the following represents the largest amount?
options: Average November value of each of the 5 holdings
November value of holdings in Northern Pacific
70% of November’s value of holdings in Southern Pacific
Average December value of each of the 5 holdings

questions.prompt: In October 2010 what fraction of the total Pacific Bond did the Northern Pacific and Pacific Mixed fund holdings represent?
questions.explanation: Northern Pacific and Pacific Mixed represent 18% + 12% = 30% of the fund. 30% = 30/100 = 3/10. Answer D.

questions.prompt: For Weeks 1 and 3, across all 5 stores combined, what was the difference (in units) between Actual and Target sales volumes?
questions.explanation: Week 1 Actual totals 20 + 30 + 25 + 15 + 5 = 95 and Target totals 15 + 20 + 20 + 10 + 10 = 75, so Actual is 20 over. Week 3 Actual totals 120 and Target totals 130, so Actual is 10 under. Answer E.

questions.prompt: Over the three week period, which Store achieved the highest sales per sales staff member?
questions.explanation: Actual sales per staff member are Redcliff (20 + 20 + 35) ÷ 8 = 9.375; Ather 110 ÷ 9 = 12.22; Wilkington 67 ÷ 5 = 13.4; Trew 41 ÷ 8 = 5.125; and Tunston 20 ÷ 6 = 3.33. Wilkington is highest. Answer C.

questions.prompt: Next year staff numbers are to be reduced by 1 at stores with 6 or less staff, and by 2 staff at all other stores. What will be the average monthly target per staff member across all 5 stores if the regional target (across the 5 stores) is £168,000?
questions.explanation: New staff counts are Redcliff 6, Ather 7, Wilkington 4, Trew 6 and Tunston 5, totaling 28. £168,000 ÷ 28 = £6,000 per staff member. Answer B.

questions.prompt: The Western Region’s overall sales (£120,000) were in a ratio of 3:2 to the Eastern Region’s sales which itself had half the sales of the Northern and Southern Regions combined. What were the total sales of all 4 Regions?
questions.explanation: If Western:Eastern = 3:2 and Western is £120,000, Eastern is £80,000. Eastern is half of Northern plus Southern, so Northern plus Southern is £160,000. Total = £120,000 + £80,000 + £160,000 = £360,000. Answer E.

questions.prompt: All sales in the three week period were based on an average £9.50 reduction in the sales price of the units sold. What was the total saving made by customers who bought units over the 3 week period (to the nearest £100)?
questions.explanation: Actual units sold total 95 in Week 1, 98 in Week 2 and 120 in Week 3, for 313 units. The saving is 313 × £9.50 = £2,973.50, which rounds to the nearest £100 as £3,000. Answer A.

questions.prompt: Which sector experienced the highest sales for Quarters 1, 2 and 3 combined?
questions.explanation: Three-quarter totals in £thousands are Telecommunications 30 + 27 + 25 = 82; Utilities 35 + 20 + 20 = 75; Manufacturing 21 + 32 + 30 = 83; Financial 25 + 29 + 30 = 84; and Retail 23 + 30 + 25 = 78. Financial is highest. Answer D.

questions.prompt: Quarter 4’s income per sector is in the same ratio as Quarter 3, and the consultancy income from the Financial sector is £33,000. What is the consultancy income from the Utilities sector?
options: Can’t tell from the data provided
questions.explanation: In Quarter 3, Utilities:Financial is 20:30 = 2:3. If Quarter 4 Financial income is £33,000, Utilities income is £33,000 × 2/3 = £22,000. Answer C.

questions.prompt: For Quarters 1 and 3 combined, which two Manufacturing sector consultants had incomes in the ratio 2:3?
questions.explanation: Quarter 1 plus Quarter 3 incomes are David £9,000, Peter £13,000, Sarah £11,500, Jane £11,500 and Harry £6,000. Harry:David is £6,000:£9,000 = 2:3. Answer A.

questions.prompt: The Manufacturing sector income from the five consultants is supplemented by the work of an associate consultant. What was the associate consultant’s income from the Manufacturing sector across Quarters 1 to 3?
questions.explanation: The chart gives Manufacturing income of £21,000 + £32,000 + £30,000 = £83,000. The five named consultants total £79,000 over those quarters. The associate therefore earned £83,000 - £79,000 = £4,000. Answer B.

questions.prompt: The total quarterly income target, starting with £115,000 for Quarter 1, increased by 20% for each subsequent Quarter. In Quarter 3 what was the difference between actual income and the target?
questions.explanation: Quarter 3 target is £115,000 × 1.20² = £165,600. Actual Quarter 3 income is (25 + 20 + 30 + 30 + 25) × £1,000 = £130,000. The shortfall is £165,600 - £130,000 = £35,600, an under-performance. Answer E.

questions.prompt: Simon and Jessica have travel allowances of 60p and 44p per mile respectively. Simon and Jessica each travel on average 25 miles and 30 miles respectively per sales visit. How much travel allowance is claimed in total by these 2 Sales Managers in August?
questions.explanation: Simon claims 70 visits × 25 miles × £0.60 = £1,050. Jessica claims 85 visits × 30 miles × £0.44 = £1,122. Together they claim £1,050 + £1,122 = £2,172. Answer D.

questions.prompt: If the percentage change in sales visits between September and October (projected) continues for November, what will Jessica and Kim’s number of complete sales visits be in November?
questions.explanation: Jessica changes from 90 to 81, a factor of 81/90 = 0.9; applying it again gives 81 × 0.9 = 72.9, or 72 complete visits. Kim changes from 62 to 70, a factor of 70/62; applying it again gives 70 × 70/62 = 79.03, or 79 complete visits. Answer D.

questions.prompt: If the margin of error on October’s projected client visits is +/- 15%, what are the ranges for each Sales Manager (rounded to the nearest whole visit)?
Jessica, who travelled 3,500 miles in July, travelled an extra 10 miles per client visit compared to Simon. What was the total number of miles Simon travelled in July?
questions.explanation: Jessica made 70 July visits, so she travelled 3,500 ÷ 70 = 50 miles per visit. Simon travelled 10 fewer, or 40 miles per visit, and made 65 visits. His total was 65 × 40 = 2,600 miles. Answer B.

questions.prompt: The average order value per client visit is £145, £135 and £125 for Simon, Jessica and Kim respectively. Which Sales Managers generate the highest and lowest order values in June?
questions.explanation: June order values are Simon 50 × £145 = £7,250; Jessica 45 × £135 = £6,075; and Kim 60 × £125 = £7,500. Kim is highest and Jessica is lowest. Answer A.

questions.prompt: Which subsidiary will pay the lowest amount in dividends (interim and final dividends combined)?
questions.explanation: Combined dividend amounts are: Subsidiary 1, (6.2 + 15.8) cents × 3m shares = $0.660m; Subsidiary 2, 19 cents × 3.5m = $0.665m; Subsidiary 3, 55 cents × 12m = $6.600m; Subsidiary 4, 25 cents × 2.6m = $0.650m; Subsidiary 5, 36 cents × 20m = $7.200m. Subsidiary 4 is lowest. Answer D.

questions.prompt: Which 2 or 3 subsidiaries had combined sales of 1,890.8 million?
questions.explanation: Subsidiaries 1, 2 and 5 have displayed sales of 1,124 + 3,334 + 14,450 = 18,908 units. At $100,000 per displayed unit, that is $1,890.8 million. Answer C.

questions.prompt: Over the next year, Subsidiary 5’s Sales are expected to drop by a fifth whilst its number of staff is expected to increase by 15%. What will be the percentage change in the Sales per member of staff from Year 1 to the next?
questions.explanation: Sales become 80% of their old value while staff become 115%, so sales per staff become 0.80 ÷ 1.15 = 0.69565 of the old level. The decrease is 1 - 0.69565 = 0.30435, or about 30%. Answer D.

questions.prompt: What is the ratio of Subsidiary 4’s interim dividend per share compared to Subsidiary 5’s final dividend per share?
questions.explanation: Subsidiary 4’s interim dividend is 15 cents and Subsidiary 5’s final dividend is 25 cents. The ratio 15:25 simplifies to 3:5. Answer D.

questions.prompt: What is the lowest average payroll per member of staff (across the 5 subsidiaries)?
questions.explanation: Payroll per employee is: Subsidiary 1, $12.7m ÷ 555 = $22,883; Subsidiary 2, $40.9m ÷ 1,722 = $23,751; Subsidiary 3, $28.9m ÷ 1,343 = $21,519; Subsidiary 4, $57.0m ÷ 2,824 = $20,184; Subsidiary 5, $435.5m ÷ 13,292 = $32,764. The lowest is $20,184. Answer E.

questions.prompt: If Profit before tax increases by 15% for Competitor B and decreases by 8% for Competitor A, what is the difference between Competitor A and Competitor B’s corporation tax payments (to the nearest £million)?
questions.explanation: Adjusted pre-tax profit is £90m × 0.92 = £82.8m for A and £112m × 1.15 = £128.8m for B. At 30% tax, payments are £24.84m and £38.64m. The difference is £13.80m, which rounds to £14 million. Answer C.

questions.prompt: Competitor B and Competitor C choose to declare their Revenues in $ and Euros respectively. What are these figures? (Use the exchange rates 1£ = $1.66; 1£ = €1.15).
options: Can’t tell from the data provided
questions.explanation: Competitor B revenue is £632m × 1.66 = $1,049.12m, shown to the nearest million as $1,049m. Competitor C revenue is £600m × 1.15 = €690m. Answer B.

questions.prompt: What would be the difference in Euros if Competitor A used an exchange rate of 1£ = €1.20, rather than 1£ = €1.15, when calculating its Profit after tax?
questions.explanation: Competitor A’s profit after tax is £63m. The exchange-rate difference is €1.20 - €1.15 = €0.05 per pound, so the reported difference is £63m × 0.05 = €3.15 million. Answer E.

questions.prompt: What was the average Gross profit across the 3 competitors (to the nearest £10million)?
questions.explanation: Average gross profit is (£128m + £148m + £147m) ÷ 3 = £423m ÷ 3 = £141m. Rounded to the nearest £10 million, this is £140 million. Answer A.

questions.prompt: Competitor C moves to a country charging 15% corporation tax and corporation tax falls to 22% for Competitors A and B. What is the total corporation tax payable for the 3 competitors (based upon the Profit before tax figures shown)?
questions.explanation: Tax is £90m × 22% = £19.8m for A, £112m × 22% = £24.64m for B, and £117m × 15% = £17.55m for C. Total = £61.99m, which is approximately £62 million. Answer A.
